summary: Defines a new VCCV control channel type for pseudowires carried over MPLS that do not use the control word. It uses the Generic Associated Channel Label from RFC 5586 to distinguish control packets from user data.

eli5.summary: A special flag marks health-check packets so they are not mistaken for ordinary traffic.

subtitle: A new way to tag pseudowire health-check packets with a reserved label, for pseudowires that run without a control word.

tldr.problem: VCCV, the control channel for pseudowires, had no good way to mark its packets when the pseudowire does not use the Control Word. The other options need IP or depend on an exact TTL, which can leak packets into the attachment circuit.
tldr.mechanism: VCCV CC Type 4 places a Generic Associated Channel Label (GAL) at the end of the MPLS label stack, followed by a Generic Associated Channel Header, so VCCV packets are recognised by the label alone.
tldr.outcome: Equipment that supports it advertises Type 4 when the Control Word is off, and the type is preferred over Types 2 and 3. It matches how MPLS-TP identifies OAM messages.

today: RFC 7708 is a Proposed Standard published in November 2015. The metadata lists no obsoleting or updating RFCs.

sections.title: Why Another VCCV Channel Type
sections.content:
The Virtual Circuit Connectivity Verification (VCCV) protocol from RFC 5085 gives a pseudowire (PW) a control channel for checking that it works. Three channel types existed. Type 1 uses the PW Control Word (CW) to tell VCCV packets from user data. Types 2 and 3 need IP encapsulation for the OAM packets.

That IP requirement conflicts with the goals of MPLS-TP (RFC 5921), which do not otherwise need IP. Type 2 does not apply to multi-segment PWs (RFC 6073), so a multi-segment PW without the CW has to use Type 3, which relies on TTL expiry. If the TTL in the PW label stack entry is set wrongly, VCCV packets will not reach the terminating provider edge and may leak into the attachment circuit.

The RFC says that simply requiring the CW is not viable. PWs without the CW are already widely deployed, some existing hardware cannot use the CW for some PW types, and some operators worry that the CW makes packets bigger.
sections.eli5: The old ways of marking check notes were either awkward or easy to get wrong. And you cannot just force everyone to use the old tag, because many trucks do not have the right holder for it.

sections.title: The Type 4 Packet Format
sections.content:
When the PW CW is not used, VCCV CC Type 4 MAY be used. The presence of a GAL at the end of the MPLS label stack tells the receiver the packet carries a VCCV message. The GAL label stack entry (LSE) MUST contain the GAL reserved label from RFC 5586, and the PW LSE is built by the usual procedures for the PW type in use.

After the GAL comes a Generic Associated Channel Header. Its first nibble is 0001, followed by a version, a reserved byte and a Channel Type, which says what kind of OAM message the VCCV message body holds.
sections.eli5: The packet gets a special label near the end that shouts 'I am a check note', and right after it a small header says what kind of check note it is.

sections.title: Load Balancing, FAT PWs and Multi-Segment PWs
sections.content:
If the LSP uses equal-cost multipath (ECMP) and some router treats special-purpose labels like ordinary labels when choosing a path, the GAL can send OAM packets down a different path from the PW data. If that is not acceptable, another VCCV type has to be used. Equipment that follows RFC 7325 leaves special-purpose labels out of the load-balancing decision, so Type 4 traffic follows the data.

For flow-aware transport (FAT) PWs (RFC 6391), a flow LSE must be present, so the GAL takes the place of the flow LSE. The packet structure is the same as the basic one, and all OAM packets then take exactly one of the possible paths.

On a multi-segment PW, the sending PE MUST set the TTL so the packet expires at the target switching PE. A switching PE that supports this MUST inspect PW packets received through TTL expiry and check whether a GAL follows the PW LSE. One that does not support it would be expected to reject the packet as malformed, so the change is backwards compatible.
sections.eli5: If the roads split into several lanes, the check note might take a different lane from the parcels. The RFC says to pick another method if that matters. On a long route with many stops, the sender sets a countdown so the note gets opened at the right stop.

sections.title: Advertising and Choosing the Channel Type
sections.content:
The VCCV capability advertisement MUST match the C-bit in the PW FEC element (RFC 4447). If the C-bit is set, meaning the CW is used, Type 4 MUST NOT be advertised. If it is not set, equipment supporting this RFC MUST advertise Type 4. So advertising Type 1 and Type 4 together is mutually exclusive. A PE MAY also advertise other types.

When the remote PE supports Type 4 and the CW is not in use, the order of preference is Type 4 (GAL), then Type 2 (Router Alert Label), then Type 3 (PW label with TTL equal to 1).

If the remote PE sees Types 1 and 4 both advertised, or the C-bit set together with Type 4, it should report the error to the operator and send a Label Release Message with the status code VCCV Type Error.
sections.eli5: Both ends say which kinds of check notes they understand and agree on the best one. If one end says something that makes no sense, the other tells the operator and refuses.

sections.title: Manageability and Security
sections.content:
Adding a fourth type means operators have one more VCCV type to manage, but it addresses the problems of Types 2 and 3. If this type is misconfigured, the PW is taken out of service and the operator is told, as described in the negotiation rules. The RFC also points out that PW data and Type 4 packets may not share fate, because of the ECMP and FAT behaviour above.

On security, the document raises nothing new beyond RFC 5085 and RFC 6073. It adds that the procedure removes the packet leaking that can occur with VCCV Type 3.
sections.eli5: Having one more kind of note to keep track of is a small cost. The new kind is safer because notes no longer slip out where they should not.

sections.title: IANA Assignments
sections.content: IANA assigned a new bit in the MPLS VCCV Control Channel (CC) Types registry: Bit 3 (0x08), described as Type 4: GAL. It also assigned a new LDP status code, 0x00000035, named VCCV Type Error.
sections.eli5: The official list of codes got two new entries: one number for the new note type and one for the 'wrong combination' error.
